results.content: # Threshold-optimized and features-fused semi-supervised domain adaptation method for rotating machinery fault diagnosis☆. In the field of intelligent fault diagnosis, domain adaptation (DA) technology achieves significant breakthroughs, particularly in reducing reliance on large volumes of labeled samples. To overcome the above challenges, a novel DA approach based on chaos sparrow search algorithm (CSSOA) optimized threshold parameters and feature fusion deep belief network (DBN) is proposed, named CSS-DADBN. Firstly, this method, by integrating pseudo-label updating with semi-supervised domain adaptation (SSDA) and employing confidence and entropy threshold parameters as corrective rules for pseudo-label filtering, along with the introduction of iterative conditions as an additional selection criterion, effectively alleviates the aforementioned issues. As a branch of transfer learning, domain adaptation (DA) approach focuses on adjusting model parameters to lessen differences between source and target domain data, thus improving the performance of models in the target domain [19], [20].

results.title: Label Propagation Algorithms in Semi-Supervised Learning
results.content: Among the many SSL techniques, label propagation is particularly useful when you’re working with graph-based data. Label propagation uses this graph structure to spread the label information from a few labeled nodes (users) to the vast majority of unlabeled nodes, creating a ripple effect of knowledge. So, while SSL GANs and VAEs excel at tasks like image synthesis or text generation, they don’t exploit graph-based structures like label propagation. In short, label propagation stands out when working with **graph-structured data** but may fall short when handling **unstructured data** where methods like self-training or generative models outperform. Because the algorithm propagates labels based on the graph structure, majority class labels tend to dominate, especially when the graph connects majority class nodes more densely. You might be wondering: “How do I construct a graph that’s actually useful for label propagation?” Here’s a simple truth — graph construction is as much an art as it is a science. Let’s quickly recap: label propagation is a powerful tool for semi-supervised learning, particularly on graph-structured data.

results.title: Intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machine via Expansive dual-attention fusion Transformer enhanced by semi-supervised learning - ScienceDirect
results.content: # Intelligent fault diagnosis of rotating machine via Expansive dual-attention fusion Transformer enhanced by semi-supervised learning. Uncertainty Bayesian deep learning SSL enhanced the proposed IFD methods. Our model excels in IFD tests, besting 10 networks on CWRU and transmission shaft data. The precise identification of faults is an essential component in the effective operation and maintenance of rotating machinery (RM). The increasing adoption of deep learning in this field is likely due to the vast amounts of automatically generated monitoring data and its robust ability to learn and detect errors effectively. To address these challenges, we introduce the Expansive Dual-Attention Fusion Transformer (EDAF-Transformer), which is trained through a semi-supervised approach using minimal labeled data. This establishes the basis of our approach to intelligent fault diagnosis, particularly under the constraints of raw vibration signals and limited labeled data availability. We then present our novel model, the EDAF-Transformer , which comprises two main components: the Expansive Dual-Attention Enhanced Modules and the 1-D Twin Global Self-Attention Transformer Encoder Module.

results.content: Semi-supervised LSTM ladder autoencoder for chemical process fault diagnosis and localization - ScienceDirect Skip to main contentSkip to article Volume 251, 6 April 2022, 117467 Semi-supervised LSTM ladder autoencoder for chemical process fault diagnosis and localization Author links open overlay panel Shuyuan Zhang, Tong Qiu * •Semi-supervised learning is innovatively introduced to deep learning-based fault diagnosis. Supervised deep learning usually works as an uninterpretable model for fault diagnosis and is deficient in analyzing which process variable information supports the fault classification result. Herein, we propose a novel semi-supervised long short-term memory ladder autoencoder (LSTM-LAE) to utilize unlabeled data and interpret variable importance in deep learning fault diagnosis and localization. Compared to conventional supervised black-box deep learning models, LSTM-LAE is novel in two major aspects: one is that unlabeled data can be utilized to promote fault diagnosis performance; the other one is that LSTM-LAE allows explicit variable importance calculation which helps to localize faults to concrete process variables. 3 different fault categories can be introduced to this process, which are cold In conclusion, this paper proposes a novel semi-supervised LSTM-LAE to take advantage of unlabeled process data and designs internal interpretable weights as variable importance to facilitate fault localization in chemical processes.
